newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs, Kyrgyz plan $120 mln hydroelectric plant.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs, Kyrgyz plan $120 mln hydroelectric plant.

text.p: The Central Asian nations of Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan plan to form an "energy pool" and build a $120 million hydroelectric power station, Kazakh Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin said on Tuesday.

Speaking to reporters at the start of an official visit to Kazakhstan by Kyrgyz President Askar Akayev, Kazhegeldin said the power station would be built on the Nurek river in neighbouring Kyrgyzstan.
He gave few details on the venture but said it required around $120 million in investment.
"Participation in the pool is a vital necessity for Kyrgyzstan," said Kazhegeldin.
Akayev and Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev also signed a series of agreements on economic and defence cooperation and swore "eternal friendship".
Kyrgyz officials had said they also hoped to secure a one-million-tonne annual oil deal with their former Soviet neighbour during the two-day visit.
